title: Comparative Evaluation of Non-Invasive Caries Detection methodsin Adolescents: Conventional Methods versus Intraoral Scanner Technology
summary:
The aim of this dental study is to determine whether caries diagnosis using intraoral scanners in adolescents shortly before treatment with fixed braces is a viable alternative to conventional diagnostic methods.
Adolescents aged 12 to 17 who are preparing for treatment with fixed braces or aligner therapy (transparent plastic splints) can participate in this study.
What is an intraoral scanner?
The use of intraoral scanners is now a widespread standard procedure in dentistry.
 Intraoral scanners are already frequently used for digital impressions of teeth and for digital imaging and measurement of the upper and lower jaw. The scanner consists of a movable handpiece with a camera connected to a computer. The handpiece and camera are used to take intraoral (three-dimensional) images of the teeth and surrounding structures. 
The images from the scanner can also be used as a diagnostic aid. Little is known about the use of scanners in preventive dentistry, including caries diagnosis and monitoring, particularly in paediatric and adolescent dentistry.
The study is being conducted at the Polyclinic for Conservative Dentistry/Polyclinic for Orthodontics at Heidelberg University Hospital. Participation in the study requires approximately 60 minutes of time and may require a separate visit to the clinic. The examination is carried out as part of a normal dental check-up. If indicated, further diagnostics, including X-rays (conventional bitewing X-rays), will be performed. No additional X-rays are required as part of the study.
 In addition, three intraoral scans (three-dimensional images of the teeth) of the upper and lower jaw will be taken using three different intraoral scanners. The intraoral scanners used in the study (Trios 4, iTero Element 5D, Emerald S with Cariosity Tip) are used for the purpose described by the manufacturer and are CE-registered as medical devices. 
The examination does not pose any health risks.
Following the dental examination, the adolescents and their legal guardians will receive information about their current oral health status and will be informed about the findings, diagnosis and treatment.
 Participants (young adolescents) and their legal guardians have the opportunity to ask specific questions about diagnostics and treatment. Following the clinical examination and patient information session, the adolescents complete a questionnaire. The aim of this is to determine which method of caries diagnosis was the most comfortable for the adolescents.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•Adolescents aged 12 years up to completion of 17 years (early permanent dentition).
•Adolescents shortly before the start of the MB phase or undergoing orthodontic treatment.
•Adolescents with ICDAS II Code 3 on at least one tooth and/or
•Adolescents requiring minimally invasive/non-invasive dental treatment (e.g. initial carious lesions, active carious lesions).
Exclusion criteria:
•Adolescents with a severe systemic disease.
•Adolescents with low caries risk (ICDAS II Code 0, ICDAS II Code 1, ICDAS II Code 2).
•Adolescents whose native language is not German.
•Structural anomalies of the teeth.
•Trauma to the teeth and/or late consequences of dental trauma.
•Objection or refusal of consent by the legal guardians.
